paper: QUERY — which query you are allowed to ask sets the leakage order

0: Which Query You Are Allowed to Ask Sets the Leakage Order
Holding the two worlds fixed and varying the admissible measurement instead
Rider University  ·  CIG-AMF formal research programme  ·  7 Lean 4 modules, 54 audited declarations, 0 sorry, axioms only {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}
20: Two fixed worlds are to be told apart from observations. We hold the WORLDS fixed and vary instead the ADMISSIBLE MEASUREMENT.
The observation density of world W at perturbation h is a finite Gaussian mixture:
Expanding in h produces coefficients Δ_j. The LEAKAGE ORDER is the least j with Δ_j ≢ 0.
Two things must be established separately, and the second is the one usually skipped:
·  the coefficients below order r cancel;
·  Δ_r ≢ 0.  'Some coefficient is nonzero' is NOT enough — the shifted Gaussian derivatives could in principle cancel one another.
WHAT IS NOT NEW  (read at theorem level)

Ho & Nguyen, arXiv:1609.02655.  Thm 3.1: singularity level r gives inf ‖p_G − p_G₀‖∞ / W_s^s(G,G₀) > 0 for s ≥ r+1.  Thm 3.3(a): minimax lower bound n^(−1/2s) for s ∈ [1, r+1), over a COMPACT parameter space.
So the phenomenon that singularity degrades the rate is PRIOR, with minimax lower bounds already proved. We credit it and do not restate it as new.

What the prior does NOT contain: the observation model is FIXED throughout — no theorem varies which measurements are legal — and no separation parameter h appears anywhere; rates are powers of the sample size n.
8: 1.  Show the same two worlds acquire DIFFERENT leakage orders under different admissible queries.
2.  Prove Δ_r ≢ 0, so the order is well defined and not an artefact of cancellation.
3.  Sandwich H² between two explicit constant multiples of h^{2r}, then convert to matching sample-complexity bounds and a two-sided regret window.
4.  Correct our own earlier note: the prior contains no h at all, so 'claiming the h-rate puts us inside the prior' was too strong.
1: STEP 1.   THE GAUSSIAN DERIVATIVES, BUILT.        iteratedDeriv_gauss,  hpoly_coeff,  hpoly_ne_zero
The degree-n coefficient of H_n is (−1/σ²)ⁿ ≠ 0, hence H_n ≠ 0 — the fact the non-vanishing argument needs.
STEP 2.   PUSH THE DERIVATIVE THROUGH THE SUM.        iteratedDeriv_fun_sum,  contDiff_component
Mathlib has the multilinear iteratedFDeriv_fun_sum_apply but no scalar-variable counterpart; this file supplies it. Smoothness of each component is DISCHARGED, not assumed.
14: The j-th derivative in h at h = 0 of the whole mixture IS the order-j level sum. This is the step the audit recorded as the one remaining piece of Q3.
18: STEP 4.   NON-VANISHING — THE HARD HALF.        levelSum_ne_zero,  mixture_coeff_ne_zero

Every term of the second sum is a polynomial against a DECAYING exponential, so it tends to 0. If T ≡ 0 then c_v* H_r(·−v*) would tend to 0 at +∞, forcing its leading coefficient to vanish — contradicting c_v* ≠ 0 and H_r ≠ 0. So the shifted Gaussian derivatives cannot conspire to cancel.
3: The chain — rate, sample complexity, regret
16: STEP 5.   THE HELLINGER SANDWICH.        hellinger_lower_from_interval,  hellinger_upper_const

The lower constant is 32, not 16 — it comes from the Cauchy–Schwarz interval bound, and the looser constant is easy to write by accident. The upper side uses an integrable Gaussian envelope and a uniform Taylor remainder, both proved: chi2_pointwise, bound_of_vanishing_derivs, envelope_integrable, gaussComp_contDiff.
STEP 6.   FROM HELLINGER TO PER-SAMPLE INFORMATION.        log_sandwich
This converts the sandwich on H² into a sandwich on the per-sample log-affinity L = −log(1−H²).
STEP 7.   MATCHING SAMPLE COMPLEXITY.        sufficient_count,  necessary_count,  ceil_suffices,  matching_rate
The two sides differ by the factor 2 of step 6 and the ratio c₊/c₋ of step 5 — both explicit, neither hidden in an asymptotic. ceil_suffices states that the integer ceiling suffices.
STEP 8.   THE REGRET WINDOW.        regret_ge_gamma_error,  lrt_regret_le,  bayes_regret_window
with γ = 13983/32768 and L_max = 2401/4096. Regret is bounded below by γ times the error probability and above by L_max times it; the window follows.
STEP 9.   THE ANALYTIC LIMIT.        ratio_tendsto_of_dominated,  hellinger_ratio_tendsto,  limit_pos_of_ae_ne_zero

A sandwich localises the ratio in [c₋, c₊]; it does not say the ratio CONVERGES. Dominated convergence along h ↓ 0 supplies the limit, and limit_pos_of_ae_ne_zero turns the pointwise non-vanishing of step 4 into a strictly positive leading constant.
15: Figure 1.  The Hellinger sandwich. Both sides have slope 2r on this log-log plot, so the ORDER is pinned, not merely bounded above. The lower constant 1/32 comes from the Cauchy–Schwarz interval bound; the upper constant J/2 from the integrable Gaussian envelope.
12: Figure 2.  Measured Bayes regret against the proved window, for two admissible measurements of the SAME pair of worlds. The shaded band is [γρ^2N/4, L_max ρ^N/2]; the black bar is a bootstrap 95% interval over 4000 repetitions per world. Both measured values land inside. The order-1 measurement needs N = 41,006 samples where the order-2 measurement needs 4,678 — the same worlds, a different legal query. Source: P33_query_actual_regret.json.
13: The leakage order is a property of the QUERY, not of the parameter space. The same two worlds, measured differently, separate at different orders, and the sample cost of restoring distinguishability follows the order through H² ≍ h^{2r}.

The chain is closed end to end and machine-checked: Gaussian derivatives built explicitly, the derivative pushed through the finite sum, the order-r coefficient shown not to vanish, H² sandwiched, converted to matching sample counts, and bracketed as regret. Step 4 is the one usually skipped and is the reason the order is well defined at all.

SCOPE — NOT ESTABLISHED.  (1) Normalising constants 1/(σ√2π) and 1/j! are dropped throughout; the dropped expressions must not be quoted as densities. (2) The cancellation statement assumes the two worlds share a level set. (3) Non-vanishing needs a strict top level; ties at the top are outside it. (4) The regret window's ends separate as N grows: it localises regret, it does not determine it. (5) No minimax statement is made — the comparison with Ho–Nguyen is a comparison of DIFFERENT objects.
